subject: LumenPay deal — feature catalyst request: conditional routing & tenant affinity
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: LumenPay deal — feature catalyst request: conditional routing & tenant affinity

Team,

Quick context: LumenPay (payments platform) is at final legal review for a multi-year Dedicated contract. They signed off on price contingent on two technical asks that are not in our standard roadmap:

1) Conditional model routing by tenant metadata (route specific customers to a higher-isolation model variant for regulated merchants).
2) Tenant affinity/warm cache reservation for a small set (10–15) of high-volume merchants to meet 50ms p95 latency.

Attached: SOW v3 and their completed security questionnaire. Key asks are summarized on page 2 of the SOW. They want a confirmation on implementation approach and an ASAP ETA (within 6 weeks) before legal will finalize signatures.

As commercial owner I need a product + eng prioritization decision with rough scope and delivery risk. Options I see:
- Fast-path: Narrow-scope implementation (routing toggle + per-tenant tag + best-effort affinity) delivered in ~4–6 weeks with feature flags and manual operational runbooks.
- Full-path: Proper model variant pinning + autoscale reservations + billing metric changes — 10–12 weeks and needs dedicated infra work.

Asks:
- Marissa: can product sign off on Fast-path acceptance criteria and a mitigations list?
- Ben: feasibility on a 4–6 week scoped delivery with existing infra, rough engineering estimate, and key blockers?
- Monica: CS input on customer acceptance testing and rollback criteria.

I flagged this as high urgency (legal will hold signature otherwise). Happy to set a short 30m sync today if helpful.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Lumen_SOW_v3.pdf, lumen_security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenPay deal — feature catalyst request: conditional routing & tenant affinity

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A few clarifying questions before we commit to Fast-path:

1) What exactly does Lumen define as the tenant metadata key? Is this an existing header/field or would it require them to change client integration? (If they have to change integration, that adds time.)
2) For affinity: do they want hard reservations (capacity reserved per tenant) or soft warm pools with SLO prioritization? The SOW language is a little loose.
3) Acceptance criteria: can we get a minimal test plan from them (sample traffic pattern, target p95, and failure-mode expectations)?

If the answers are: "existing metadata header" and "soft warm pools" and they provide a 3-case test plan, product could greenlight a Fast-path with the following mitigations baked in: feature flag, canary for 2 tenants, rollback to shared pool, and a 30-day post-commit stability window.

Ben — can you sketch a rough implementation plan for Fast-path (what we ship, what is manual ops vs automated) and a ballpark FTE estimate? If the estimate is >3 engineer-weeks we should have a quick cost/benefit conversation with the customer (we may need a short-term activation premium).

Marissa
Senior PM, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 10:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenPay deal — feature catalyst request: conditional routing & tenant affinity

Marissa / Rishi — quick feasibility note from eng side.

High level: Fast-path is feasible but comes with known limitations. Quick bullets:
- Routing toggle: straightforward. We can accept a tenant-level tag (X-LUMEN-TENANT: <id>) at the gateway and route to a specific model variant or a routing tier. ~2 engineer-weeks to wire up request tagging + routing policy evaluation + feature flag.
- Affinity/warm cache: implementing a soft warm pool / priority queueing mechanism is doable with minimal infra changes (~3–4 engineer-weeks). Hard reservations (strict capacity reservations per tenant) require scheduler and billing changes and are a 8–12 week project.
- Observability: we need work to attribute latency and cost to tenant buckets and add a tenant-level dashboard (2 engineer-weeks).

Risk/notes:
- Fast-path will be manual in operations for initial rollout (we will not have autoscale reservation automation). That means on-call ops involvement during the first 30 days and an ops runbook.
- Service impact: tenuous if traffic spikes — we should put a contractual traffic cap for any tenant in the Fast-path SOW.

Estimate (Fast-path MVP): 6–8 engineer-weeks total across runtime and infra (split across 3 engineers over 4 weeks) + 1 PM. If Lumen is willing to pay an activation premium/engineering surcharge we can re-prioritize.

Next steps asked of Sales/Product:
1) Confirm whether Lumen can supply the tenant metadata without client-side changes.
2) Decide if we accept the manual ops window and traffic caps in the SOW.
3) Confirm whether they are open to a 30-day canary where we keep a modest surcharge.

Ben
Engineering Lead, Runtime — Redwood Inference

On Tue, Feb 14, 2028 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Victor Hsu <victor.hsu@lumenpay.com>, LumenPay Legal <legal@lumenpay.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Feb 2028 13:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenPay deal — feature catalyst request: conditional routing & tenant affinity

Hi Rishi / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers below:

1) Tenant metadata: we can send X-LUMEN-TENANT as a header from our gateway with no client changes.
2) Affinity: soft warm pools are acceptable to start. We absolutely want a path toward hard reservations but we can accept the staged approach.
3) Test plan: attached is a short test plan with sample traffic shapes (see page 3). Target p95 for the 10 merchants is 50ms end-to-end; we understand the initial canary and are comfortable with a surcharge during the 30-day window.

We need sign-off on scope and a commitment date so legal can finalize signatures. Our target is to go live before the end of March (ideally by March 26).

Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, LumenPay

Subject: Re: LumenPay deal — feature catalyst request: conditional routing & tenant affinity

Team / Aisha — thanks for the rapid feedback. Summarizing agreed path and asks so legal can proceed:

Agreed path (Fast-path MVP):
- Accept X-LUMEN-TENANT header as routing key.
- Implement routing toggle + tenant tag evaluation and soft warm pools for up to 15 merchants.
- Manual ops runbook for first 30 days; contractual traffic cap per tenant (to be included in SOW).
- 30-day canary window with a 10% activation premium for the customer.

Engineering ask: Ben, can you confirm capacity to start work on Monday Feb 21 and commit to the 4–6 week Fast-path timeline given the 6–8 engineer-weeks estimate? If we need the activation premium to secure more eng headcount, please call that out and we'll present to the customer.

Product/CS ask: Marissa / Monica, please confirm the minimal acceptance tests and the rollback criteria we should put in the SOW. Legal will expect those in the SOW appendix.

Aisha — if you can confirm the traffic cap numbers we can draft a narrow SOW amendment and circulate to legal today. If legal needs a draft text I can attach our suggested clause.

I'll schedule a 20m call Monday morning to lock scope if that works for everyone.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Lumen_SOW_v3.pdf, lumen_security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx
